title: SLO query templates + labeling sheet (rollout auto-rollback)
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-10 (Allison)

Purpose
- Working sheet for the auto-rollback on SLO breach project.
- Defines: (1) required metric labels (monitor identity contract), (2) query templates for latency + error SLO monitors, (3) example time windows, (4) checklist to create monitors per service/route.

Notes / assumptions
- Query syntax below is PromQL-ish (matches what we use in the internal SLO toolkit + observability pack). Adjust for the target backend if needed.
- We are standardizing identity across hosted + dedicated + private where possible; some labels will be unavailable in on-prem until telemetry backfill scripts land (see INT-3310 + ENG-2322).
- Auto-rollback uses these monitors by ID, so label consistency matters more than exact threshold values here.

====================
TAB 1 — Canonical labels (monitor identity contract)
====================

A) Required labels for rollout-related SLO monitors (minimum set)

| Label key | Required? | Example | Notes / rules |
|---|---:|---|---|
| env | Y | prod | Must be one of: prod, staging (no dev monitors consumed by rollout-controller). |
| service | Y | inference-gateway | Logical service name (not k8s deployment). Must match service registry naming. |
| route | Y | /v1/chat/completions | Canonical route name. Prefer normalized path template, not full URL. |
| region | Y | us-east-1 | Cloud region or on-prem region alias. Must match routing region string. |
| customer_tier | Y | hosted_free, hosted_paid, dedicated, private | Values align with billing tier + isolation tier. Avoid customer-specific values here. |
| model | Y | llama-3.1-70b-instruct | Model family/name (not version build SHA). |
| model_version | Y | 2025-02-05.1 | Serving version used in routing config. Must match rollout controller version identifiers. |
| deployment_mode | Y | hosted, dedicated, private | Used to separate SLOs that differ materially. |

B) Optional / recommended labels

| Label key | Recommended? | Example | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| tenant_id | R (only for per-tenant SLOs) | tnt_9c12 | Avoid unless explicitly required; high cardinality. For auto-rollback we typically operate at (tier, region, route, model, version). |
| cluster | O | prod-use1-07 | If needed for infra debugging; do NOT include in monitor identity used by rollout decisions unless there’s a strong reason. |
| sdk | O | python, js | Useful for segmentation. Not part of monitor identity. |
| request_type | O | streaming, non_streaming | If we need split SLOs later; for now keep out to avoid monitor explosion. |
| status_code | O | 500 | Used on raw metrics; monitors should aggregate. |

C) Label normalization rules (so queries don’t drift)
- route: normalize to stable template (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, not /v1/chat/completions/ or full host).
- model/model_version: must match rollout controller routing config values.
- customer_tier: use fixed enums; avoid “enterprise_customer_name”.
- region: must match the control plane region string exactly.

Owners
- Label contract: Allison Grant
- Pipeline enforcement: Nadia Rahman
- Dashboard/monitor packaging: Sergio Costa

====================
TAB 2 — Metric names used by templates
====================

| Metric | Type | Emitted by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| redwood_request_total | counter | inference-gateway + model-server | Total requests. Must include status_class label (2xx/4xx/5xx) OR status_code label. |
| redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket | histogram | inference-gateway | Latency histogram; must include route, region, model, model_version, customer_tier. |
| redwood_request_tokens_total | counter | inference-gateway | Optional. Useful for token-weighted SLOs later; not used by rollback today. |
| redwood_monitoring_scrape_lag_seconds | gauge | telemetry | Used to gate on staleness/outage. |

Open issue (tracking)
- INT-3310: some services missing model_version label on duration histogram.

====================
TAB 3 — Query templates (latency)
====================

Legend
- ${...} indicates template variables; the rollout controller will substitute based on policy scope.
- Most monitors are created per: (env, service, route, region, customer_tier, model, model_version, deployment_mode)

A) P95 latency (primary rollback signal)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Required labels in metric | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| slo:latency_p95:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model}:${model_version} | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}"}[${rate_window}]))) | env, service, route, region, customer_tier, deployment_mode, model, model_version | rate_window=2m; evaluate over 10m and 30m rollups | Use 2m rate window to reduce spikiness; policy can require breach across N consecutive evaluations. |

B) P99 latency (optional, typically dashboard-only)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| slo:latency_p99:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model}:${model_version} | histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}"}[${rate_window}]))) | rate_window=2m | Do not use for auto-rollback until we validate stability across low-traffic routes. |

C) Baseline comparison: candidate vs stable (ratio)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| slo:latency_p95_ratio_canary_to_stable:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model} | (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${candidate_version}"}[2m])))) / (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${stable_version}"}[2m])))) | 10m | Used for “must-be-worse-than-baseline” policy semantics. Gate with min traffic (see Tab 5). |

Implementation note
- If stable_version is unknown, fallback to comparing against last-7d p95 for the same tuple excluding model_version (TBD; likely too complex for v1).

====================
TAB 4 — Query templates (error)
====================

A) 5xx rate (primary rollback signal)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Required labels | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| slo:error_5xx_rate:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model}:${model_version} | (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}",status_class="5xx"}[${rate_window}]))) / (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}"}[${rate_window}]))) | env, service, route, region, customer_tier, deployment_mode, model, model_version, status_class (or status_code) | rate_window=2m; evaluate over 10m and 30m | Prefer status_class="5xx" to avoid exploding series. If only status_code exists, use status_code=~"5.." and aggregate. |

B) Timeout rate (optional, but useful for latency->error shifts)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| slo:error_timeout_rate:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model}:${model_version} | (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}",error_type="timeout"}[2m]))) / (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}"}[2m]))) | 10m | Depends on consistent error_type labeling (not universally present today). Track coverage before enabling. |

C) Baseline comparison: 5xx rate candidate vs stable (delta)

| Monitor name template | Query template | Suggested eval windows | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| slo:error_5xx_rate_delta_canary_minus_stable:${service}:${route}:${region}:${customer_tier}:${model} | ((sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${candidate_version}",status_class="5xx"}[2m]))) / (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${candidate_version}"}[2m])))) - (((sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${stable_version}",status_class="5xx"}[2m]))) / (sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${stable_version}"}[2m])))) | 10m | Delta tends to be more stable than ratio when baseline is near-zero, but needs guardrail for low traffic. |

====================
TAB 5 — Guardrail / health-of-monitor queries (required for automation safety)
====================

A) Minimum traffic (gate rollback decisions)

| Purpose | Query template | Suggested thresholds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ensure enough requests observed for tuple before evaluating p95 or error rate | sum(rate(redwood_request_total{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}",model_version="${model_version}"}[2m])) | Example: >= 1 rps for 10m window (tier-dependent) | This is policy-controlled in rollout-controller (minTraffic). Monitor should exist to aid debugging + dashboards even if gating is handled in code. |

B) Monitor staleness / telemetry outage

| Purpose | Query template | Suggested thresholds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detect scrape lag beyond acceptable bound | max(redwood_monitoring_scrape_lag_seconds{env="prod",service="${service}",region="${region}"}) | Example: > 120s => treat verdict as UNKNOWN | Rollout controller should not rollback on UNKNOWN; it may fail-open or fail-closed per policy (see ADR-0148). |

C) Data completeness sanity check (label presence)

| Purpose | Query template | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Quick check to confirm model_version label is present on histograms | count by (model_version) (redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",service="${service}",route="${route}",region="${region}",customer_tier="${customer_tier}",deployment_mode="${deployment_mode}",model="${model}"}) | If model_version is missing/empty, escalation to telemetry pipeline owner. |

====================
TAB 6 — Example windowing + alerting defaults (informational)
====================

These are NOT final SLO values; just example evaluation windows we’ve been using to test stability.

| Signal | Short window | Long window | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency | 10m | 30m | 10m catches hard regressions quickly; 30m reduces false positives on bursty traffic. |
| 5xx rate | 10m | 30m | Same; use 2m rate for smoothing. |
| min traffic | 10m | n/a | Align with decision window (don’t evaluate if you don’t have enough data). |
| cooldown after rollback | n/a | 30–60m | Prevent flapping; allows caches/warmup to settle after revert. |

TODO (SRE feedback)
- Validate whether we should run both windows simultaneously (require both breached) vs require sustained breach in short window only.

====================
TAB 7 — Monitor creation checklist (per service/route)
====================

Checklist — create monitors for a given service/route tuple
1) Identify the routing scope
   - service = ?
   - route = ? (normalized)
   - deployment_mode(s) = hosted / dedicated / private
   - customer_tier(s) = which tiers need distinct thresholds
   - regions = list of active prod regions for this route

2) Validate metrics exist with required labels
   - redwood_request_total has: env, service, route, region, customer_tier, deployment_mode, model, model_version
   - redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket has same label set
   - status_class available OR status_code available
   - If missing: file INT ticket and add to ENG-2322 migration plan

3) Create / verify monitors (per region + tier + model + model_version)
   - latency_p95 monitor
   - error_5xx_rate monitor
   - min_traffic query (even if just for dashboard)
   - scrape lag monitor for region/service

4) Confirm identity naming matches contract
   - Monitor name includes: service, route, region, customer_tier, model, model_version
   - Monitor labels/tags mirror the same tuple
   - No cluster/node/pod labels in identity

5) Dashboard wiring (observability-pack)
   - Add panels for p95, error rate, request volume, and verdict timeline
   - Add links: rollout page, runbook, and “monitor query debug” view

6) Dry run / validation
   - Pick a known traffic slice; compare computed p95 to existing latency dashboards
   - Simulate a small threshold breach in staging (or use synthetic harness) and ensure monitor triggers correctly

7) Sign-off
   - Observability: Sergio
   - SRE: Aisha or Miles
   - Control plane consumer: Benji

Known pitfalls (from earlier rollouts)
- Low traffic routes: p95 becomes noisy; must gate on min traffic.
- Missing model_version label: causes stable + canary traffic to be merged; breaks baseline comparison.
- region naming mismatch (e.g., use1 vs us-east-1): monitor becomes orphaned and never found by rollout-controller.

Open questions
- Do we need separate monitors for streaming vs non-streaming for /v1/chat/completions? (would require request_type label coverage; currently inconsistent)
- Dedicated customers: do we treat tenant_id as part of identity for rollback? (product request exists; high cardinality risk)

Change log
- 2025-01-17: Initial draft templates (Allison)
- 2025-01-29: Added baseline comparison templates + min traffic gating notes (Miles)
- 2025-02-04: Updated label keys to match ADR-0147 wording; added staleness/UNKNOWN guidance (Nadia)
- 2025-02-10: Revised status_code vs status_class guidance; clarified not to include cluster/pod labels (Sergio)
